These are the Client Terms: for people who book appointments or hold a portal account with a business that uses KinesioCal. Running a practice on KinesioCal? The Provider Terms of Service are yours.

KinesioCal Client Terms of Use

Last updated 11/12/2026

1. Who This Covers

These Client Terms of Use ("Client Terms") apply when you book, pay for, or manage appointments with a business that uses KinesioCal ("KinesioCal," "we"), including through the business's public booking page (which the business may link from its own website), through email confirmations, or through a KinesioCal client account. By booking, you accept these Client Terms.

Three parties are involved:

  • You — the client booking a service.
  • The business — the licensed massage therapist or other provider you are booking with. The business is your service provider. It sets its prices, policies, and availability, holds your records, and is responsible for the service you receive.
  • KinesioCal — the software the business uses to run its schedule and records. We are not a party to your appointment, we do not provide services, and we do not employ or vouch for any business. We do not handle your money: when you pay, your payment goes through the business's own payment processor (such as Stripe) directly to the business, and KinesioCal never receives or holds your funds. A refund the business issues from inside the Service is paid from the business's own processor balance, not by KinesioCal. We process your booking and record information on the business's behalf.

You must be 18 or older to create a client account. A parent or guardian may book for a minor under their own account; the business is responsible for the minor's record and for the guardian consent it requires, and will tell you what it needs before the appointment.

2. Booking, Payment, and Cancellation

The business's policies govern your appointment. Deposits, cancellation windows, no-show fees, late arrival, refunds, and tipping are set by the business and shown to you before you confirm. KinesioCal does not set or enforce them and cannot issue refunds on a business's behalf; contact the business directly.

Payments. Card payments are processed by Stripe. The business is the merchant; its name appears on your statement. KinesioCal never sees your full card number and takes no portion of your payment. Disputes about a charge should go to the business first.

Accurate information. You will book under your own legal name and provide your own working email address and phone number, and you will complete any intake or health form honestly. The business relies on that information to contact you, to send confirmations and reminders, and to treat you safely. You may not book under a false or borrowed name; enter an email, phone number, or address that is not yours, including the business's own contact details, a placeholder such as example.com, or a disposable address; or create a second account to avoid a block. If you do, the business may cancel the appointment, decline service, charge any cancellation or no-show fee under its policies, and block you, and KinesioCal may close your account under Section 4. Neither the business nor KinesioCal is responsible for confirmations, reminders, receipts, or notices that fail to reach you because the contact details you gave were wrong.

ID checks. Any business may ask you to show a government ID matching your booking name when you arrive, for the practitioner's safety, whether or not it warned you in advance. Businesses can choose to display an ID-check notice at booking; a business that does not display the notice has not given up the right to ask. The business, not KinesioCal, is asking for and reviewing your ID; KinesioCal does not collect or store ID images or numbers, only whether a check was completed. If you decline to show ID when asked, the business may decline to provide the service and apply its cancellation policy.

Messages. By booking, you agree to receive appointment confirmations and reminders by email. We do not send text messages. A business's newsletters are on by default and can be turned off under Notifications in your account; confirmations, reminders, and receipts are not affected.

Mobile and outcall services. If you book a service at your home or another location, you agree to provide a safe, clean, private space; to be present and sober; and to allow the practitioner to end the session at any time if they feel unsafe.

Booking for a minor. A parent or guardian who books for a minor is responsible for the minor's information and conduct under these Client Terms.

Who to contact. For anything about an appointment, a charge, a refund, your records, or how a business treated you, contact the business; KinesioCal cannot change a booking, issue a refund, or alter a business's records. Contact KinesioCal at KinesioCalendar@gmail.com only for problems with your KinesioCal account or login, a Safety Network challenge, a privacy request we can act on, or to report conduct by a business that violates these terms or the law. Support hours are posted in the Support panel of the app; we respond during those hours and may use automated and AI-assisted tools to handle requests.

3. Prohibited Conduct

The businesses on KinesioCal are licensed professionals. You may not use KinesioCal, any business's booking page, contact information published on KinesioCal, or any appointment booked through it to:

  • request, suggest, hint at, or offer payment for sexual contact or any sexual or illicit service, whether in a booking note, intake form, message, phone call, or in person, and whether by direct words, slang, euphemism, or coded language;
  • during an appointment booked through the Service, expose yourself, touch a practitioner inappropriately, or make sexual remarks. KinesioCal cannot observe what happens in a session and does not supervise appointments; conduct during an appointment is reported to us by the business, and we act on those reports under Section 4;
  • harass, threaten, stalk, or discriminate against a practitioner or business, or repeatedly book and cancel to disrupt their schedule;
  • book under a false name, use someone else's payment method, or use more than one client account to avoid a block, hide your booking history, or appear to be a different person. Creating a duplicate account by accident is not a violation; if you discover you have more than one, tell us at KinesioCalendar@gmail.com and we will help you consolidate them;
  • attempt to find or contact a practitioner's personal information, home address, or personal social media through the Service;
  • interfere with the Service, scrape it, or attempt to access another person's records;
  • make a report about a business or practitioner that you know or should know is false, or for the purpose of retaliation or harassment. Reports made honestly that turn out to be mistaken are not a violation, but a knowingly false report of sexual misconduct or illegal activity against a licensed practitioner can end their career, and we treat it as seriously as the conduct it alleges: your account may be closed, your identity may be disclosed to the business so it can pursue its own remedies, and you are responsible for the harm caused.

A practitioner may end any session immediately, without refund, if you engage in any of the above. A business may also, at its sole discretion and without giving a reason, block you from booking with it or contacting it through the Service.

4. What Happens If You Break These Rules

Suspension and bans. A business may block you from its booking page at any time, for any reason. If a business reports that you solicited sexual or illicit services, or engaged in harassment, assault, or threats, KinesioCal may also suspend or permanently close your client account and bar you from booking with any business on the platform.

No new accounts. If you are suspended or banned, you may not create another account or book under another name, email, phone number, or payment method to get around it. Doing so is a further violation. Any account created to circumvent a ban is void and will be closed. To enforce this, KinesioCal compares the email address and phone number given at signup and at booking against hashed records of banned users, and keeps those hashed identifiers after your account is closed for that purpose — by default for five years, longer where the conduct warrants it. KinesioCal does not promise that every circumvention attempt will be detected.

Reporting to authorities. Soliciting sexual services from a massage therapist is a crime in Indiana, and most other states. If a business reports that you solicited sexual or illicit services, made threats, or assaulted a practitioner, KinesioCal and the business may report you to local law enforcement and provide your booking details and account information, without notice to you. Nothing in these Client Terms limits a practitioner's right to call the police.

Your responsibility for costs. You are responsible for actual losses you cause. To the business, that includes its cancellation or no-show fees under its policies, the cost of a session ended early for prohibited conduct, and chargebacks you file in bad faith. To KinesioCal, if you use the Service to solicit sexual or illicit services, harass or threaten a practitioner, or impersonate another person, that includes the cost of investigating and responding to your conduct, cooperating with any resulting law-enforcement or licensing-board inquiry, and repairing harm to the platform's reputation, including documented public-relations and customer-retention expenses, together with reasonable attorneys' fees and collection costs.

Fairness. We know false reports happen. A ban across the platform is not automatic; see Section 6 for how reports are reviewed and how you can challenge a network block.

5. The Safety Network

KinesioCal includes a Safety Network that lets businesses warn each other about clients who have been blocked. Here is how it works.

A business can block you. Any business may block you from its own booking page at any time, with or without giving a reason. That block applies only to that business and is entirely that business's decision: KinesioCal will not review, undo, or remove a block a business has placed on its own booking page, and you cannot appeal it to us. If you believe a block was a mistake, contact the business directly. Each business decides whether to use the Safety Network at all.

A business can share a block. When a business blocks you, it may also share the block with the Safety Network under one or more categories: no-call no-show, sexual harassment, threats or violence, unsafe dwelling, policy violation, non-payment, theft, maltreatment of staff, or other. The share records whether the business reports a single offense or repeated behavior, and whether it attached supporting documentation; a share without documentation is marked that way everywhere it appears.

Other businesses choose what to accept. Participation is each business's choice. A participating business is matched only with other participating businesses within the alert radius it sets around its own location (25 miles unless it changes it, between 1 and 500), and it sets which categories it will import and whether it will import shares that have no documentation. A business that does not participate, is outside the sharing business's reach, or does not import the category or documentation level of your block, is not affected by it. Your email address and phone number are stored as a one-way hash for matching; the original values are encrypted and readable only by the business that shared the block and by KinesioCal moderation.

No information travels until you try to book. Your block is not broadcast. When you attempt to book with a participating business in range using the same email address or phone number, that business's log records the categories, single or repeated, whether documentation exists, the date, and any different name or contact details you used in the attempt. It does not receive the name of the business that blocked you, that business's notes, or its documentation. If the business has chosen to import that category (and, for a share without documentation, to import undocumented shares), your booking is refused, you see a generic message that online booking is not available, and you are added to that business's own blocklist, which it controls and can remove at any time. If it has not, your booking goes ahead and the match is only logged.

How long a share lasts. A share in the sexual harassment or threats or violence categories stays live until the business withdraws it or a review removes it. A share in any other category stops reaching other businesses one year after it was filed unless the business deliberately renews it. A business may withdraw a share at any time, and a withdrawn share cannot be re-shared.

What the Safety Network is not. It is not a background check, a public record, or a credit report. Your individual records are not sold or shared with businesses outside the platform. KinesioCal may publish de-identified statistics about the Safety Network as a whole, such as how many blocks are shared by category or region; these never identify you or any business. Safety Network records about you, including the category of any block and any documentation the business attached, may be shared with law enforcement and with professional licensing or regulatory boards, either in response to legal process or when KinesioCal or a business reports suspected solicitation, threats, assault, or conduct involving a minor, as described in Section 4.

6. Challenging a Safety Network Block

You have the right to ask KinesioCal to review the network share of any block. You cannot challenge the original business's own decision to block you; that is its choice and it stands regardless of the outcome. A successful review ends every live share about you, so that other businesses no longer receive it, and retracts the blocks other businesses had imported from those shares; their logs show the block as retracted by platform review. A block a business placed by its own decision is unaffected, and a business remains free to block you itself.

How to request a review. Sign in to your client account and use the Booking restriction review card, which appears when a network share matches your verified contact details or when you have a review case. Give your name, email address, and phone number so we can match the share, and tell us in your own words what happened. The form asks you to confirm that you have read these Client Terms and the platform's policies, that you have not violated a business's policies, propositioned or assaulted a practitioner, and are current on what you owe the business, and that everything you submit is accurate. If you cannot use the card, email KinesioCalendar@gmail.com and we will take the request that way.

What happens next.

  1. We notify every business whose live share matches your contact details that a review has been requested. That notice carries your name and the statement you wrote, so the business can respond; do not put anything in your statement that you do not want the business to read. The business may add a comment or supporting documentation for our moderators until the review is decided.
  2. There is no fixed window. A business whose share has no documentation on file is told that the review is expected to go against it unless it adds some before we decide.
  3. KinesioCal moderation reviews the shares, their documentation, and your statement against the categories claimed, and may contact the sharing businesses for confirmation or details. There are two outcomes: upheld, and the shares stand; or removed, and every live share matching your contact details stops reaching other businesses, cannot be re-shared by those businesses, and the blocks other businesses imported from it are retracted. Nothing is deleted on a removal: the reports, their documentation, and the review stay on file so that a later review of the same person can see them.
  4. The result appears on the Booking restriction review card in your account, with its date. We do not give you the business's evidence or identify the business.

Several shares at once. A review looks at every live share that matches your contact details together, whoever filed them. Independent businesses reporting the same conduct is something our moderators weigh, but there is no automatic rule that a number of reports ends your right to a review.

After a removal. If a business later shares a new block about you, you may request a review of that one on its own. A later review may also reverse an earlier removal if new information shows a report was accurate; the businesses concerned are told either way.

Timing. We review requests as promptly as reasonably possible. Review time depends on how many requests are pending and on how quickly the businesses respond, and we do not commit to a fixed timeline. While a review is pending, the share remains in effect.

Final decisions. KinesioCal's decision on a network share is final within the platform. It does not affect any legal rights you or the business may have.

7. Your Privacy, Our Limits, and Contact

Platform decisions are internal and final. Reviews of reports, challenges, account closures, and bans are conducted internally by KinesioCal, using the information available to it and at its discretion. These are decisions about who may use the Service and how, not legal findings. KinesioCal's decision on any such matter is final as to your use of the Service; we are not obligated to reopen a review, provide our reasoning beyond what these Client Terms describe, or hear further appeals. These decisions do not determine any legal rights or liabilities between you and a business, and they do not prevent you or any business from pursuing legal remedies in a court or other forum with jurisdiction. By using the Service, you agree to this process for platform decisions.

Your records, and their use as evidence. What you do through the Service is recorded: bookings, cancellations, booking notes, intake answers, and the outcome of any report or challenge involving you. You may download a copy of your records at each business you booked with from your account at any time, and you may use it for any lawful purpose, including as evidence in a legal proceeding. To have a business's record of you removed, ask that business; KinesioCal never alters a business's records at a client's request. A business may likewise export its own records. KinesioCal does not release one party's data to another on request; a business seeking your records, or you seeking a business's records, must obtain them from that party or through legal process served on KinesioCal as described in the Privacy Policy. Records are provided as they exist in the Service, without certification, and KinesioCal does not act as a witness or give opinions about them except as required by legal process. You should expect that your conduct on the Service, and any report about it, may be produced in a court or regulatory proceeding.

Sharing your records between businesses. If you have an account and book with more than one business on KinesioCal, you may give one of them read-only access to parts of the record another holds about you, from Your data & invoices in your account: your contact details, your booking-form answers, your appointment history, or the notes that business chose to show you. Notes a business keeps for its own staff are never included. If a business has deleted your profile or has closed, only your appointment history with it remains, and that is all you can share from it. Each business keeps its own record; sharing changes or merges nothing, the receiving business sees the shared information in a separate view marked as shared by you, and you can stop a share at any time, after which that business no longer sees it. Only you can share your records this way; no business can share them with another business on your behalf or ask KinesioCal to. Each share and each stop is recorded in both businesses' activity logs.

Your privacy. The business you book with holds your records and decides how they are used; ask the business for its privacy notice. KinesioCal processes your information only to run the business's schedule and records, and as described in the KinesioCal Privacy Policy, shown alongside these terms. We never sell your personal identifying information or health information. KinesioCal uses AI tools to help build the Service and to help handle support requests; the Privacy Policy explains what those tools receive and the limits we place on them. For access to or deletion of the records a business holds about you, contact the business; if you cannot reach them, email KinesioCalendar@gmail.com and we will relay your request. Whether you have your own KinesioCal account matters. If you created an account, it is independent of any business, and for your account and the contact details held on it KinesioCal deals with you directly: we will notify you ourselves of any data breach affecting them, and you can exercise your privacy rights over them with us rather than through a business. If a business closes, your account, login, and contact details remain until you close the account with Close my account in your profile, and your appointment and payment history with that business becomes part of your account: the services, dates, amounts and receipts, and nothing else the business wrote about you. That history is then the only copy KinesioCal holds; it stays until you close your account and is deleted 30 days after that, and we tell you so before you confirm. If a business deletes your profile while you hold an account, your account keeps showing your appointment and payment history with it. If you have only ever booked as a guest without creating an account, the business's record of you is the only data KinesioCal holds about you, and it is removed on the same schedule as the business's other records when that business closes. Information in a closed account may be deleted 90 days after closure. Closing your account removes your login and the contact details on your account, and, 30 days later, any history a closed business left to you; each business you booked with keeps its own record of you, and you would contact that business to have it removed. An account that was created but never used to complete a booking may be deleted 90 days after it was created. If your account sees no activity for 24 months, your login may be deactivated and you revert to a guest client: the records each business holds about you are unchanged, and you can book as a guest or create a new login at any time. Activity means any action on your account or records by you or a business, including a booking, a charge, a sign-in, or a change to your record. We will attempt to email you before deactivating a login. Individual records, such as a past appointment, are archived after 18 to 24 months and may be permanently deleted 30 months after the date of the record, whether or not anyone has viewed them in the meantime.

Safety Network data. A share in the sexual harassment or threats or violence categories stays live until the business withdraws it or a review removes it; a share in any other category stops reaching other businesses one year after filing unless renewed. After a share ends, the report, its documentation, and any review of it stay on file with the business that filed it and with KinesioCal moderation, so that a later review of the same person can see them; they are not deleted on a schedule today, and we will update this paragraph when a retention period is set. Identifiers used to prevent ban circumvention are kept in hashed form after a platform ban, by default for five years and longer where the conduct warrants it.

Health information and HIPAA. Intake and health forms you complete are collected by the business for your care and stored in the Service. KinesioCal is not currently HIPAA-certified or HIPAA-compliant and does not offer HIPAA compliance or a Business Associate Agreement to businesses. We are building the Service with the intent of becoming HIPAA-compliant in the future, using the HIPAA security standards as our reference, and the Privacy Policy explains what is in place today. We treat your health information as health information and protect it accordingly, and we never sell your personal identifying information or health information. Whether HIPAA applies to a business depends on that business, not on KinesioCal. Ask the business if you have questions about how it protects your health information.

KinesioCal's software. The Service, including public booking pages, is owned by KinesioCal, LLC. You may use it only to book and manage your own appointments. You may not copy, reverse engineer, or extract its code or design; use bots, scripts, or automated tools to book, cancel, or monitor appointments; scrape practitioner, business, or availability data; or probe or test its security. Doing so may result in account closure and, where it causes harm, liability under Section 4.

KinesioCal's limits. KinesioCal provides software only. We do not screen, license, supervise, or guarantee any business or practitioner, and we are not responsible for the services you receive, for any injury, or for a business's policies or conduct. Practitioner licensure can be verified with your state licensing board. To the fullest extent permitted by law, KinesioCal's liability to you for anything arising from these Client Terms is limited to \$100.

Changes. We may update these Client Terms. The current version is shown in the app wherever these terms are accepted and on its Legal page; material changes take effect 30 days after posting.

General. These Client Terms and the Privacy Policy are the complete agreement between you and KinesioCal about your use of the Service; your agreement with any business is separate. If any part of these Client Terms is found unenforceable, that part will be limited to the minimum extent necessary and the rest will remain in effect. KinesioCal's failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it. You may not transfer your account or these Client Terms to anyone else; KinesioCal may assign them to a successor as described in the Privacy Policy. The sections on prohibited conduct, consequences, the Safety Network, platform decisions, records, KinesioCal's limits, and governing law survive the closure of your account.

Disputes with KinesioCal. These Client Terms are governed by Indiana law and the Federal Arbitration Act. Disputes about an appointment, a charge, or a business's conduct are between you and the business; this paragraph covers only disputes between you and KinesioCal.

  1. Tell us first. Before starting any proceeding, email KinesioCalendar@gmail.com describing the problem and what you want. We will try to resolve it with you for 30 days.
  2. Small claims first. If the dispute is not resolved informally and the claim qualifies for small-claims court, it must be brought there, in Lake County, Indiana, or in the county where you live, and not in arbitration. If a claim that qualifies for small claims is filed in arbitration, either party may require that it be moved to small-claims court, and no arbitration fees are due until it is determined that the claim cannot proceed there. KinesioCal is a small Indiana company. If a claim is brought anywhere other than Lake County, you agree that KinesioCal may participate by telephone, video, or written submission to the extent the court allows, you will not object to or oppose a request by KinesioCal to appear remotely, and you will confirm your consent to the court if asked. Nothing in this paragraph limits the court's own rules.
  3. Individual arbitration. Any dispute that does not qualify for small claims, or that a small-claims court declines to hear, will be resolved by binding individual arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Consumer Arbitration Rules, by video conference or telephone. If you ask for an in-person hearing, it will be held in your county as the Rules provide, but you agree that KinesioCal and its witnesses may participate by video conference or telephone and that you will not object to or oppose that participation. Documents may be exchanged and filed electronically. KinesioCal will pay all arbitration fees beyond the consumer filing fee set by those Rules. The arbitrator may award you anything a court could, on an individual basis. If the arbitrator finds that a claim was frivolous or brought for an improper purpose, such as harassment, the arbitrator may require the party who brought it to reimburse the other party's arbitration fees and reasonable costs, as the Rules permit. Otherwise each party bears its own attorneys' fees unless a law that applies to the claim provides for them.
  4. No class actions. You and KinesioCal agree to bring claims only in an individual capacity, not as a plaintiff or class member in any class, consolidated, or representative action, and the arbitrator may not consolidate claims of more than one person. If this sentence is found unenforceable for a particular claim, that claim will be heard in court, not arbitration, and the rest of these Client Terms remain in effect.
  5. Opt-out. You may opt out of arbitration and the class waiver by emailing KinesioCalendar@gmail.com within 30 days of first accepting these Client Terms, stating your name and the email on your account. Opting out does not affect anything else.

If more than 25 similar claims are filed against KinesioCal by the same law firm or coordinated group, the parties agree to resolve them in staged batches, with the first 10 arbitrated as test cases before further filing fees are due.

Contact. KinesioCal, LLC, KinesioCalendar@gmail.com.
